extracted.intended_audience: judge advocates, military attorneys, convening and reviewing military commanders, and other military legal practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and legal principles governing the constitution, jurisdiction, records, proceedings, sentencing, review, and remedial actions for courts-martial and inferior military tribunals (summary, regimental, garrison). Primarily addresses what defects are fatal, when proceedings are void, remission/clemency principles, and authority/responsibilities of convening and reviewing officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voidness of court-martial convened without jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Court-martial proceedings are void when the order assuming to convene it is null and void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A court convened by an officer without authority is without jurisdiction and its proceedings cannot operate to separate a soldier from the service. (C. 1645; C. 13103 cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record must show members and judge advocate were duly sworn
rubrics_metrics.description: A record which fails to show that the members of the court and judge advocate were duly sworn is fatally defective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits by the judge advocate and president that they were sworn do not cure the defect because they are not part of the proceedings; remedy may include setting aside sentence and recalling a discharge. (C. 9600; C. 8197; C.15330).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of challenge must be shown in record
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the record of trial fails to show that the accused was allowed an opportunity to exercise his right of challenge, the proceedings are fatally defective and the sentence is void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to record opportunity to exercise challenge has led to holdings voiding sentences. (C. 13297; 22163; 18764).

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges must allege essential elements of the offense
rubrics_metrics.description: Omission to state essential elements (e.g., that accused had received pay and allowances in fraudulent enlistment) renders the proceedings fatally defective as not constituting an offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where essential allegations are omitted, charges may be amended and accused retried before a legally constituted court; such retrial is not a second trial within the meaning of the relevant article of war. (C. 11998).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective record may only be amended by the court itself when reconvened
rubrics_metrics.description: If the court has not been dissolved it may be reconvened to amend its record to conform to the actual facts; a defective record returned for correction can only be amended to conform to the actual facts and by the court itself on revision when duly reconvened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interlineations by judge advocate on a returned record are unauthorized and invalid. (A.G.O. 1900; Court Martial Manual, 1898 cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum composition requirement of court (five members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a court, though reduced by absence of members, operation of challenges, etc., to below five members, yet proceeds with and concludes the trial, its further proceedings, including finding and sentence, are unauthorized and inoperative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceeding with fewer than required members renders findings/sentences invalid. (R.2,450; C.18764).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval null if soldier already discharged
rubrics_metrics.description: The approval of a sentence is null and void where the soldier in question has already been discharged from the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sentence approved after a soldier's discharge cannot be legally effective. (C.24658).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency or contradiction of prosecution evidence may warrant remission
rubrics_metrics.description: When the prosecution introduces limited or contradicted evidence (e.g., only one witness contradicted on material point) and the accused is convicted, it may be proper to remit unexecuted portion of sentence on account of failure of proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remission may be recommended pending execution where proof is weak. (R.53,644).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of distinct offense not charged is unauthorized
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to find guilty of a minor included offense cannot justify convicting the accused of an offense entirely separate and distinct in nature from that charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding someone guilty of an offense not alleged and not included in the charge is unauthorized and may warrant remission. Examples: finding guilty of absence without leave when charged with abandoning post before enemy; finding of article 40 offense under article 39 charge. (R.11,274i; R.11,276; R.34,569; C.12375; 18764).

rubrics_metrics.name: Insanity during trial nullifies proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: If an insane soldier is shown by the record to have been insane pending the trial, the proceedings and sentence should be declared null and inoperative in orders; if insanity is shown after approval, the sentence should be remitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record evidence of insanity pending trial requires setting aside; if raised later remission is appropriate. (R.55,563).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied promise to accomplice witness not to prosecute
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an accomplice offers and is admitted to testify for the Government, he is called under an implied promise that no proceedings will be taken against himself and that pardon will be favorably considered if he makes full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such an accomplice later is prosecuted and convicted, it has been recommended that his sentence be remitted. (R.11,590; R.14,259).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive or exceptional punishments are subject to remission
rubrics_metrics.description: Punishments which are excessive and exceptional for the offense (e.g., carrying a loaded knapsack every alternate hour) are excessive and remission of the unexpired term is recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraordinary physical punishments beyond ordinary penal consequences may be reduced. (R.26,520).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court must consider written extenuating statements offered with guilty plea
rubrics_metrics.description: Where with a plea of guilty the accused offers a written statement setting forth material circumstances of extenuation and the court takes no testimony or apparently ignores the statement but convicts and sentences, this constitutes reasonable ground for remission of part of the punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to consider extenuation submitted in writing may justify remission. (R.20,120,127,177; other citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignorance in failing to exercise right of challenge may warrant remission
rubrics_metrics.description: The failure of the accused through ignorance to avail himself of his right of challenge is a proper ground for remission in whole or part of the sentence or even for disapproval of the proceedings; but it does not affect legal validity of the sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignorance may be equitable ground for clemency though not jurisdictional invalidation. (C.10793).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clemency/review: remit when recommended or when evidence weak or dependency shown
rubrics_metrics.description: When members recommend clemency and reviewing authority does not mitigate, it is good policy to remit a portion of confinement after the sentence has been partially served; likewise when distressing dependency is shown or new evidence weakens the conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remission may be appropriate on clemency recommendation, dependency, or materially weakened evidence. (C. M. Nos. 69337, 70631; C.29064).

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss of record does not impair enforcement after regular termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have regularly terminated and sentence has been confirmed and ordered executed by proper reviewing authority, loss of the record afterwards does not impair the judgment or enforcement of the penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executed and confirmed sentences remain enforceable even if the record is later lost. (R.9,238).

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts must be lawfully constituted and within authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings of unprecedented or unauthorized courts (e.g., civilian inmates convened as a court-martial) are void ab initio; the statute empowering a body to be 'subject to the rules and articles of war' does not itself confer authority to constitute such courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts composed of persons lacking lawful authority to act as a court-martial render sentences inoperative. (R.30,286; C.12817; C.20120).

rubrics_metrics.name: Convening authority must be proper rank/position
rubrics_metrics.description: A court convened by an officer lacking proper convening authority (e.g., lieutenant colonel in command of a department convening certain courts) may be illegal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain convening acts by particular ranks were held illegal in cited cases. (C.16710; P.142,438).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of regular officers on volunteer officer trials may be improper
rubrics_metrics.description: For trying volunteer officers, general courts-martial composed partially or wholly of regular officers are illegally constituted even if those officers hold volunteer commissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition of the court must respect statutory/organizational rules for the class of officers tried. (C.7895; C.5654).

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts-martial are executive instrumentalities not part of judiciary
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts-martial are creatures of the Executive power; though transient and summary, their judgments rendered within limited jurisdiction are as legal and valid as other tribunals and are not ordinarily subject to review by U.S. or state courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictional questions may be reached by habeas corpus but the range of inquiry is limited; if jurisdiction exists, collateral review is restricted. (R.1,451; multiple citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executed legal sentences are final and not subject to executive rescission
rubrics_metrics.description: When a legal sentence adjudged by a court-martial has once been duly executed, it is irreversible and cannot be rescinded or modified by executive authority of pardon vested in the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only remedies for injustice from an executed sentence are new appointment to the Army by the President or legislation by Congress for relief/indemnity. (R.36,274; R.41,638; many citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere irregularities do not reopen an executed and confirmed case
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere irregularity in proceedings—prejudice in evidence admission, biased members, unjust finding, or excessive dismissal—cannot cause a reopening of the case where the sentence is legal and has been legally confirmed and executed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irregularities short of absolutely fatal defects do not permit reopening; executive or congressional power to nullify remains limited. (R.20,302; 26,462; 28,457; 34,634; other citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Late challenge to weight/credibility is not permitted after promulgation
rubrics_metrics.description: After the reviewing authority has acted on a case and his action has been promulgated in orders, it is too late to urge invalidity based on weight of evidence, credibility of witnesses, or other matters calling for exercise of judgment or discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges to discretionary determinations after promulgation are barred. (C.5654; C.11509; C.17386).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-martial only has jurisdiction over military offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: A court-martial sentence is illegal when the offense committed is not a military one because the court has no jurisdiction over non-military offenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictional limits as to subject matter can render sentences illegal. (C.1989).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regimental courts lack jurisdiction to redress certain officer wrongs
rubrics_metrics.description: A regimental court-martial has no jurisdiction under the 30th article of war to redress a wrong which can only be righted by punishment of the officer concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain disciplinary/administrative wrongs against officers are not cognizable by regimental courts. (G.855).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to act on proceedings when command devolves to president of court
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, after a garrison court had tried cases but before action, the command devolved upon the officer who had been president of the court, that officer may legally act upon the proceedings unless higher commander action is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception applies when the higher commander's action is not mandated by the relevant article of war. (R.43,268).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying rules for general courts to inferior courts where practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions restricting convening when the convening commander is accuser (articles 72 and 73) are expressly for general courts, but the same principle should be applied to inferior courts where it can be done without serious embarrassment to the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though not mandatory for inferior courts, the principle of impartial convening is recommended when feasible. (R.34,353; R.35,138; R.42,231).

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 103 limitation applies only to general courts-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition of article 103 (limitation) relates only to prosecutions before general courts-martial; it does not apply to trials by inferior courts or to courts of inquiry which may be convened without regard to elapsed time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules of limitation do not apply to inferior courts or courts of inquiry; hear complaints under article 30 notwithstanding time. (R.42,213; C.18772).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary courts cannot issue attachment for civilian witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary court is not empowered to issue process of attachment to compel the attendance of a civilian witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary courts lack authority to compel civilian witness attendance via attachment. (P.51,468).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary courts lack jurisdiction over capital offenses
rubrics_metrics.description: An enlisted man is not triable by a summary court for violation of the twenty-first article of war (capital cases), as such cases exceed its jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary courts' jurisdiction is limited; capital offenses and other specified classes are excluded. (C.6186; C.7392; C.10946; others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary court officer is executive officer responsible for vouchers
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary court officer is the executive officer of the summary court in the same sense that the judge advocate is the executive officer of a general court-martial, and is charged with securing vouchers regarding witness fees, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative responsibilities for summary courts mirror those of judge advocates for general courts. (C.7890; C.13418).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post commander must personally sign and date action on inferior court records
rubrics_metrics.description: The post commander should personally and with his own sign manual act on the records of inferior courts-martial convened by him, and should include in his action the date of approval, as forfeitures of pay operate only from that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal action and dating avoid disputes over effective date of forfeitures. (C.854).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing authority may require summary court to reconsider sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: The post commander, being the reviewing authority and without whose approval the sentence cannot be carried into effect, may require a summary court to reconsider a sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing commanders retain supervisory power over summary court sentences. (C.6042).

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-appointment to summary court contrary to spirit of statute
rubrics_metrics.description: Although not expressly forbidden, a commanding officer appointing himself to serve as the summary court is contrary to the tenor and spirit of the summary court act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-appointment is discouraged as inconsistent with statutory intent. (C.18121).

rubrics_metrics.name: When accuser composes the 'court' different trial forum required
rubrics_metrics.description: When the 'court' consists of the second in rank and he is the accuser, the case is to be tried by the post commander; when the 'court' consists of the post commander and he is the accuser, the case is to be tried by a regimental or garrison court-martial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism to avoid conflict of interest in appointing trial forum. (P.56,279; C.635).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and reach of summary court appointments (who may convene)
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary court act allows the commanding officer of garrisons, regiments, detached battalions, companies, etc., to appoint a summary court of one officer to try enlisted men and provides that when only one commissioned officer is present he shall hear and finally determine such cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to provide trial capability under all service conditions; applied to surgeons in command of hospitals, division surgeons, commanders of independent ambulance companies, and hospital ship commanders. (C.856; C.4966; C.4931; C.14427).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanding officer of brigade post may centralize summary court appointing power
rubrics_metrics.description: The commanding officer of a brigade post has authority as convening officer of a summary court to retain within himself the appointing power for all summary courts within his command and may organize temporary battalions for jurisdictional purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If he does not exercise the authority, appointing power, including review, passes to regimental commanders by operation of law. (C.22592).

rubrics_metrics.name: Department commander's duty to supervise inferior court proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A department commander must supervise proceedings of regimental and garrison courts-martial transmitted to headquarters; if a material error, defect, or omission is discovered, he should bring it to the attention of the proper inferior commander; fatal defects should lead to orders declaring the sentence void, non-fatal errors may be remedied by remission of unexecuted punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supervision includes distinguishing fatal vs. non-fatal defects and directing appropriate corrective or remedial steps. (R.35,174).

rubrics_metrics.name: Company commander may punish minor derelictions administratively
rubrics_metrics.description: A company commander under the control of the commanding officer of the post is authorized to dispose of derelictions within the jurisdiction of an inferior court by requiring extra tours of company or post fatigue unless the soldier demands trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders may use non-judicial corrective measures to enforce discipline. (C.3589; C.19701; C.20051; C.21211).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commanders not required to court-martial every dereliction
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanding officers are not required to bring every dereliction of duty before a court for trial; they should endeavor to prevent occurrence by admonitions, withholding privileges, and other steps necessary to enforce discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of administrative discipline is encouraged where appropriate. (C.19701; C.20051).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement date of confinement
rubrics_metrics.description: Confinement imposed by sentence of court-martial shall be considered as commencing at the date of the promulgation of the sentence in orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule (General Order 21, Headquarters of the Army, 1870) replaced earlier practice of counting from delivery to prison officer. Delaying commencement until prisoner receives notice would reinstate prior abuses. (R.30,150; G.18165).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative nature of successive confinement sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: When a soldier at two successive trials is sentenced to confinement, the sentences will be held cumulative when both are approved on the same day or when the soldier is serving one sentence when brought to trial and receives another confinement sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Execution of cumulative sentences: the second sentence will commence when the pending confinement terminates; principle applies even where prisoner escapes and later reenlists/deserts and is reconvicted. (R.34,449; C.1608; C.1609; C.12402; many citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Escaped prisoners must serve unexecuted portions upon capture
rubrics_metrics.description: When a military prisoner escapes, upon capture he must serve the unexecuted portion of his sentence; this applies whether escape occurred during trial, after sentence but before approval, or during execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One hundred and third article of war does not prevent a captured escaped prisoner from serving remaining sentence. (G.14767; C.1812; other citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prison authorities may not open prisoners' letters without consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Prison authorities have no right to open and inspect letters addressed to or sent by prisoners without the consent of the writer; they may, however, retain such letters unopened until parties are tried or released, or disposed of under judicial process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Privacy of prisoners' correspondence preserved absent consent or judicial process. (C.2469).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of sentence during execution lacks precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: The suspension of the sentence of a court-martial before or during its execution is without precedent; a post commander is not authorized to suspend execution of a sentence by good behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities have consistently held such suspension improper; post commanders lack authority under the relevant article of war to grant suspensions. (C.8838; R.30,115; C.20797; C.27738).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remission alters sentence for good-conduct computation
rubrics_metrics.description: A remission of part of a sentence of confinement leaves the reduced sentence as though it were the original, and the prisoner is entitled to good-conduct time on the reduced sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After remission, the reduced term is treated as the operative sentence for good-conduct credit. (R.37,490; P.44,66).
